newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs catch up with Bunds after auction.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs catch up with Bunds after auction.

text.p: Belgian OLOs ended firmer on Monday though beneath session highs, with the 10-year benchmark spread over Germany returning to Friday's closing levels once the monthly OLO auction was out of the way.
Dealers predict the spread will stay at least around current levels, and possibly even narrow one or two basis points more by the end of the week.

The 2006 OLO ended yielding 5.96 percent, down from 5.99 at Friday's close. Its premium over Bunds returned to 11 bps after widening to 12 ahead of the auction where the Treasury netted 14.315 billion francs from sales of March 2001 and 2007 OLOs.
Dealers predicted prices would be well supported at least until January because the prospect of paying tax on end-of-year capital gains kept investors reluctant to take profits yet.
Looking ahead into 1997, Belgian brokerage Petercam said in a research pamphlet that European bonds were looking expensive compared to U.S. bonds and a switch might be appropriate.

The brokerage also noted that there was frequently a downward correction at the start of the year, mainly because of emissions of new bond issues and by the policy of banks to create capital gains at the start of the year - especially in a low interest rate environment.
